tagline: Over Hardscrabble Pass to a valley that keeps its lights low.
intro: From Pueblo, Highway 96 skirts Pueblo Reservoir, passes through Wetmore and climbs into the San Isabel National Forest over Hardscrabble Pass at 9,085 feet. Then it comes down into the Wet Mountain Valley at Silver Cliff and Westcliffe, under the Sangre de Cristo Range. A second leg, Highway 165, turns south through the forest past San Isabel to Rye and Colorado City.

The Ute came this way first, then Spanish and American explorers, trappers, homesteaders and ranchers. Silver Cliff had 5,040 people in 1880, the third largest town in Colorado. It has about 600 now, and with Westcliffe it turns its lights down for the stars.

moments.title: Silver Cliff
moments.text: The Geyser mine on the hill north of town was once the deepest in Colorado. Eastern stock promoters ran it through two bankruptcies, and it never made a profit.

moments.title: Westcliffe
moments.text: Locals keep a free observatory in an old building whose roof rolls off to open a 14-inch telescope to the dark sky overhead.

moments.title: Bishop Castle
moments.text: Jim Bishop began a family cottage here in 1969. He covered a water tower in rock, the neighbors said it looked like a castle, and he kept building.
